tasks.short: Prepare, administer and grade tests and assignments

steps.what: Prepare tests and assignments, answer keys and grading criteria
Administer tests and assignments and collect identifiable student responses
Score closed-response items against the teacher-verified answer key and inspect exceptions
Grade open responses, evaluate progress and approve final marks and feedback

tasks.design: Configure native answer-key scoring in {LMS} for suitable closed questions. The teacher checks scoring behaviour, marks open responses and approves the exact final results in {OTHER}, the pupil record system; no model evaluates students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated answer-key comparison can consume marking time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native quiz scoring can apply explicit verified keys without interpreting open responses.
tasks.still_hard: Write a valid assessment, interpret unusual responses and judge progress.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise reasoning that a fixed key does not capture.
tasks.altitude: The teacher can avoid repetitive closed-item scoring while retaining final assessment judgement.

reach.learn: Distinguish answer-key correctness from evidence of learning

evidence.claim: Closed-item answer-key scoring is a native LMS configuration pattern; its local time benefit remains unmeasured.

assumptions: Teacher creates item_id, accepted answers, point weights and assessment_version in s1 and tests examples; full preparation time remains.

Students produce original responses under the existing assessment process. S2 includes teacher identity checks, collection and any necessary transfer. The proposal uses native digital closed-item responses; paper transcription or ambiguous responses remain manually scored with no assumed saving.
S3 remaining eight baseline units cover inspecting flagged responses and verifying scoring on a teacher-selected sample; any key defect triggers rescoring and manual checks before finalisation.
Test native quiz configuration first. No automatic release of marks, ability grouping or placement decision is introduced.
unknowns: What fraction of marking time concerns eligible closed items
Which native quiz functions are approved
research_questions: Does key-based scoring reduce marking time after setup, exception checks and final review are included?

already_counted.description: Grade open responses and approve final results

incremental.description: Maintain question versions and regression examples
Maintain approved quiz settings and access

approvals.approved_version: Teacher approves exact per-pupil results revision linked to response set, assessment version and key version before recording final marks; changes require rescoring and renewed approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=25+25+8+30=88; gross=12%; minus 2 focal upkeep gives 10% net. Low: scoring already exists or paper/open responses dominate. High: eligible closed marking shrinks; preparation, administration and open-response judgement retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set and communicate clear learning objectives

steps.what: Establish clear objectives for lessons, units and projects against curriculum requirements
Communicate objectives to students and clarify what successful learning will involve

tasks.design: Keep the selection of objectives and explanation of their meaning with the teacher, using existing {DOCS} and {LMS} materials. No new drafting tool is proposed for this task because deciding the right learning target and checking pupil understanding remain central.
tasks.previous_blocker: A clear objective must reflect curriculum intent and what this class is ready to learn.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing goal resources support the decision; generated wording alone does not establish a gain.
tasks.still_hard: Choose an achievable but worthwhile objective and communicate it clearly.
tasks.human_edge: Explain why the objective matters and address pupils’ misunderstandings.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains control over objectives and their explanation.

evidence.claim: Goal-based lesson suggestions exist in Snappet, but do not establish saved time selecting and explaining this class’s objectives.

assumptions: Teacher reads current requirements and assesses readiness within s1; no clean curriculum mapping or pupil-readiness feed is assumed.
Broader course-outline drafting is a separate planning view and its potential saving is not repeated here.
Existing tools remain unchanged, so additional upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Which curriculum and existing objective resources the department uses
research_questions: Can pupils explain the learning objective and recognise evidence of achieving it?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=55+45=100. Objective judgement and student explanation retain effort; no saving is imported from another preparation task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe and evaluate pupil development and performance

steps.what: Observe students’ performance, behavior, social development and physical health in context
Evaluate observations and identify concerns or support needs within the teacher’s role

tasks.design: Keep direct observation and evaluation with the teacher, consulting existing {OTHER} pupil records where authorised. No model diagnoses pupils or infers emotions, health or motives.
tasks.previous_blocker: Observations are situational and evaluation can affect pupils significantly.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest establishes record tools rather than a replacement for teacher observation.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a pattern from an isolated event and know when specialist support is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Understand context and listen before making an assessment.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains observation and referral responsibility.

reach.task: Review concerns based on factual observations
reach.learn: Separate description, interpretation and referral questions

evidence.claim: Pupil records can hold context, but they do not replace direct observation and professional evaluation.

assumptions: Teacher produces observations in s1 with full time retained; no prestructured behavior or health feed is assumed.
S2 includes brief evaluation notes; maintaining formal records and producing reports are separate administrative tasks, with no saving credited here.
No new application or data flow means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which referral pathways and record permissions apply
research_questions: Do evaluation notes distinguish observed facts from interpretations clearly enough for specialist review?

incremental.description: No new evaluation or monitoring system

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=70+30=100. Observation and evaluation retain their effort; no administrative saving is invented inside this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and conduct balanced learning activities

steps.what: Choose activity goals, materials and constraints for a balanced programme
Draft activity sequences balancing instruction, demonstration, observation, questioning and investigation

loop.purpose: Propose a feasible sequence of subject-learning activities
loop.input: Teacher-produced goal, time and material brief without pupil identifiers
loop.output: Timed sequence with goal links and opportunities for investigation
loop.check: Teacher verifies subject accuracy, goal relevance, feasible timing and materials, and that students actually have opportunities to observe and question
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; teacher writes unsuitable parts
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse an approved sequence first; adapting a new combination of activities requires semantic drafting

steps.what: Approve and conduct activities, adapting instruction and work time to student responses

tasks.design: Use an approved {LMS} or {DOCS} assistant to propose a sequence from the teacher’s brief. The teacher checks the final plan, supplies materials and conducts the activities with full responsibility for classroom response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Combining suitable activities into a balanced sequence involves repeated drafting.
tasks.enabler_now: Goal-based activity suggestions and measured preparation benefits exist, though local performance needs testing.
tasks.still_hard: Judge educational value and manage investigation safely in the actual setting.
tasks.human_edge: Respond to questions and turn unexpected results into learning.

ambition.what: Compare feasible activity sequences before choosing one.

tasks.altitude: The teacher gains draft options, with unchanged delivery and safety responsibility.

reach.task: Review balance and goal alignment of activity plans
reach.learn: Check that investigation opportunities are substantive

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts classroom activities for lesson goals.
The digest reports a secondary science-teacher trial with reduced preparation time; its result is not a measure of this whole activity-delivery task.

assumptions: Teacher produces goal_codes, duration, material availability and activity constraints in s1; all brief capture and judgement remain in its 10% share.
Missing constraints require manual clarification. Approved source activities are reused before generating anything; no pupil data is required.

Only sequencing draft work changes. Existing preparation, conducting and supervising activities remain fully counted; live instruction overlaps the dedicated teaching task and must not be added twice in a role roll-up.
unknowns: Which approved assistant and activity library are available
How much sequence drafting is reusable today
research_questions: Does drafting shorten preparation after subject, safety and feasibility checks are included?

already_counted.description: Review draft sequence for educational fit and feasibility

incremental.description: Maintain activity briefs and record unsuitable suggestions

approvals.approved_version: Teacher approves exact activity-sequence revision and brief before classroom use; changed activities, constraints or materials require renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=10+7.5+75=92.5; gross=7.5%; minus 1 focal upkeep gives 6.5% net. Low: existing sequences are faster or drafts fail checks. High: draft sequencing shortens while goal selection and live activity work retain effort; teaching overlap is non-additive.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Native closed-item scoring and activity drafts can reduce bounded preparation work while observation, educational judgement and student contact remain human.
reach: Review assessment validity with instructional coordinators
skills_to_grow: Verify answer keys and assessment versions
role.ambitious_version: Spend less time on repeated marking mechanics and activity drafting while keeping teacher control of objectives, marks and delivery.
